summary: 1938 52-ft timber tower in the yard of the Pine Ranger Station near Halfway, Oregon; emergency use only, fenced; record height corrected.

facts.design: 52-ft timber tower (register: open timber; firelookout.com: treated timber) with a 7x7 ft observation cab and catwalk

access.note: On the grounds of the Pine Ranger Station, a Forest Service office. A fence now surrounds the tower to keep climbers off it.

visit.trail_note: About two miles southeast of Halfway, on the Pine Ranger Station grounds. A 2023 visitor suggested asking a ranger onsite during visiting hours. A fence keeps people off the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says open timber and firelookout.com says treated timber; both describe the same 52-foot timber tower with a 7x7 cab.

corrections.why: Both the register and firelookout.com give the tower as 52 feet (about 15.8 m); 2.1 m does not match the structure

notes_for_editor: Thin record: no staff lists, fires or construction records were found beyond the 1938 build date. The Living New Deal page on CCC construction at the Pine Ranger Station returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Height: record's 2.1 m is wrong; 52 ft is consistent across the register and firelookout.com. Elevation: register 2,566 ft vs 2,600 ft on firelookout.com and the 2013 visit; the 2,600 figure is probably rounded to the nearest hundred feet, but no source says so. Access and status are an informal emergency-use situation at an active Forest Service office; the story keeps climbing discouraged. The Roaming Civic and cherylhill pages are visitor accounts, not agency records.
